KRI-MY-MSME-20260525.claim: Independent Malaysian research (KRI with MDEC) describes widespread front-facing digital adoption but weak backend integration, and support ecosystem fragmentation; macro evidence alone does not identify a specific callable recurring operator gate.

KINTONE-MY-20260325.claim: Cybozu/Kintone reports Malaysian expansion including Malay localization and CRM Suite to integrate SME administrative and relationship workflows; company offering evidence, not proof of universal coverage.

MDEC-BDI-CURRENT.claim: Malaysia's Business Digitalisation Initiative already provides SME digital maturity assessment, financing channels and expert business advisory via an existing public-private service ecosystem.

BCG-SEA-LOGISTICS-20260730.claim: BCG describes 2026 SEA logistics cross-party workflow discontinuities: single-company AI improvements often lose value at manual partner handoffs; this is aggregate research, not proof of an independent dispatch or booking permission.

LOCUS-SPOT-20260518.claim: Locus markets a system precisely for spot vehicle procurement (vendor registry, structured RFQs, qualified vendor ranking, vehicle assignment and tracking), describing messaging-based workarounds; vendor's illustrative operational scenarios are not independently validated buyer transaction records.

HAULIO-ASEAN.claim: Haulio describes an active ASEAN haulage collaboration and real-time fleet, manpower and equipment management platform; public footprint is not proof that every carrier/country/corridor is serviced.

JETRO-CHINA-ASEAN-20260319.claim: JETRO 2026 research documents Chinese companies expanding across Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia including manufacturing and data infrastructure; context for replenishment, not direct procurement demand.

ZKH-Q1-20260521.claim: ZKH reports an existing large MRO procurement platform with specialized industrial SKUs, digital product matching and international service growth supporting outbound Chinese manufacturers; it does not establish exact local SLA in each ASEAN site.

FMM-2026-H1.claim: Malaysia Federation of Manufacturers' 1H2026 industry conditions publication reports raw-material costs and supply chain disruptions as major surveyed challenges; aggregate cost pressure is not a paid site-specific MRO RFQ.

examined_formations.title: SEA logistics 3PL faces a peak-demand spot-vehicle procurement event -> qualified compatible carrier capacity and trackable handoff
examined_formations.observed_partial_flow: Independent aggregate BCG study reports cross-party manual process boundaries, while incumbent Locus documents message-based spot sourcing as part of its exact commercial offering. The specific example in Locus marketing is illustrative, not a confirmed public procurement unit.
examined_formations.counterparty_surface: Truck/capacity providers exist through carrier and haulage networks, but no independent live free-to-route vendor inventory or action permission was independently established.
material_contradictions: Messaging workaround persists but current commercial vendors explicitly sell this workflow
3PL contracts and capacity owners retain vehicle booking rights; a neutral shared rail is not publicly callable
No publicly bound repeatable buyer procurement event, quote authority, or net operator economics

examined_formations.title: Malaysian microenterprise grows beyond chat and spreadsheet operations -> integrated backend order/customer/finance records
examined_formations.observed_partial_flow: KRI identifies backend integration remains shallow despite front-facing adoption. Kintone already packages localized application integration/CRM workflows and MDEC operates public-private advisory/financing access for small firms.
examined_formations.counterparty_surface: Local digital integrators and software providers are accessible, but no excluded subgroup's independent right or public trigger for a distinct multi-provider routing transaction is established.
material_contradictions: Aggregate low adoption does not prove lack of integration software
Customization and change management are expert/service work unless a repeatable missing coordination right is evidenced
MSME adoption survey is population-level, not named payer intent

examined_formations.title: China-outbound manufacturer's ASEAN production site enters recurring MRO restock or unexpected downtime -> compatible supplies plus local fulfillment
examined_formations.observed_partial_flow: JETRO shows active China-outbound manufacturing expansion; FMM reports generic cost/disruption pressure, and ZKH reports existing outbound-Chinese-client MRO supply and specialized AI-supported procurement, without proving exact independent urgent-order leakage at a named ASEAN factory.
examined_formations.counterparty_surface: Manufacturers, local industrial merchants and existing global procurement/fulfillment networks exist; precise part identity and on-site fit may require expert diagnosis and local stock verification.
material_contradictions: Industrial pressure and international expansion do not bind an unpaid procurement event to an independent operator
Large incumbent coverage does not prove every urgent last-mile part is resolved; conversely an unsolved local stockout is not publicly shown
Exact compatible part and site-SLA require qualified procurement verification; no independent standardized authority or provider availability established
